newsitem.title: UK: Rolls says close to sale of steam power units.
newsitem.headline: Rolls says close to sale of steam power units.

text.p: Aero-engines and industrial power group Rolls-Royce Plc said on Thursday it was close to selling both of its steam power generation businesses, namely Parsons and the International Combustion.

"There are several bidders for both...and we are confident that we are going to sell both of the businesses and that we will make some announcements in the next few weeks," chairman Sir Ralph Robins told Reuters.
Robins also said the company was making progress in its attempt to sell Canadian subsidiary Bristol Aerospace and hoped to make an announcement "probably in the next few weeks."
He said the Winnipeg-based aircraft maintenance and rocket manufacturer has annual sales of around Can$60 million and employs about 1,000 people but was not considered a core business.
"It does a little bit of engine (overhaul) business for us and also for others but it's mainly in the air frame and rocket business," he said.

Rolls put Parsons and Combustion up for sale in July last year, when it said it wanted to exit the large steam power generation business, and said it would close the businesses if it could not sell them.

Earlier today, the company announced it made a 28 million pound pre-tax loss last year after booking in the 248 million pounds of provisions and write-offs detailed last year to cover its withdrawal from steam power.

But it said operating profits from its core aero-engines and industrial power businesses rose to 242 million pounds from 178 million pounds in 1995, boosted by strong order books. Annual sales excluding businesses to be sold rose to 4.05 billion pounds from 3.34 billion pounds a year ago. -- Greg Mahlich, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
